html:
Pharaoh of Egypt for 66 years, from 1279 to 1213 BCE, and the most celebrated king of the New Kingdom. Later Egyptians called him the Great Ancestor, and nine later kings took his name.

Early in his reign he fought the Hittites for Syria. At the Battle of Kadesh in 1274 BCE he was nearly trapped; the result was a draw, which his temples proclaimed a great victory. About fifteen years later he signed the Egyptian and Hittite peace treaty, one of the earliest known, with copies in both languages. He later married a Hittite princess.

He built more than any other pharaoh: a new capital at Pi-Ramesses in the Delta, his temple the Ramesseum at Thebes, and the rock temples of Abu Simbel, one of them for his chief queen Nefertari. He fathered dozens of children and outlived many of them. His mummy is in Cairo. The Greeks knew him as Ozymandias, the name of Shelley's poem.
